Analysis complete and delivered to `plans/sdd/V6-remediation/delivery-capacity-design.md` (read-only; no source authored, no tests/builds run).

## Bottom line
**The existing single-file delivery-journal format cannot host bounded-memory rollover in place — it requires a reviewed, version-gated migration.** I show exact evidence and a concrete implementation path.

## Why (four reader invariants, each anchored to one file replayed from zero)
1. **Dense per-file arrivals from 1 — the hard blocker.** `loadFrom` rebuilds `arrivals[session]` from the one file and enforces `lease.ArrivalSeq == arrivals[session]+1` starting empty (`delivery_lease.go:562-566`). A segment continuing a session mid-sequence fails immediately; the reader has no way to be seeded with prior arrivals.
2. **Fixed chain seed.** Chain seeded at constant `deliveryChainSeed`; `sealInBounds` requires an empty journal's chain to equal that seed (`delivery_seal.go:174-179`). A segment continuing the prior chain (needed for whole-history tamper-evidence) is unrepresentable; independent per-segment chains would let an archived segment be dropped undetected.
3. **Whole file in memory + one position seal per file** — no "K archived + 1 active" concept.
4. **Idempotency consults only the in-memory `j.leases`** (`:347-353`) — no on-disk fallback for archived nonces.

Plus: an old binary opening a rolled-over store sees only the active segment and would **reassign arrivals / re-mint ObservationIDs** for archived nonces — the two forbidden outcomes. (ObservationID is deterministic in `(session, arrivalSeq)`, arch §0.1, so preserving arrival continuity + the `nonce→lease` binding is exactly what keeps identity stable.)

## Implementation path (smallest compatible; a migration)
Segment files each within the existing 64 MiB/65536 caps, **reusing the v2 seal unchanged per segment** (per-file tamper detection intact); a sealed **manifest** (per-segment chain seed + a version old readers refuse) as the whole-history tamper spine; a sealed **arrivals checkpoint** to seed per-session arrivals across the boundary; a sealed **per-segment sorted nonce→ObservationID index** for bounded-memory late-copy idempotency; **reader-first/writer-second rollout** (the v1→v2 seal precedent); and an additive extension of the backup watch-list. No limit raised, no journal deleted, no identity forgotten, no arrival reassigned.

## Honest limit stated
Bounded **memory** is achievable; bounded **storage** is **not** under "never forget an identity / never reassign arrivals" — archived segments and indexes grow monotonically forever (on-disk, archived, backup-able, not in RAM). A bounded-storage design would need a retention window the task forbids.

Two shared durable-data decisions returned to main: (1) accept the version-gated segmented migration; (2) confirm the unbounded-disk/bounded-memory trade is the intended contract. SP20-D4's carry row stays open.
